Subject: June 24 incident: impact summary, timeline, and remediation for BrightHealth

Hi Maria / BrightHealth ops team —

I wanted to follow up with a concise, customer-facing summary of the partial service availability issue you experienced on June 24 and outline what we’ve done and what to expect next. Thank you for the quick reports and patience while we investigated.

Summary (what happened)
- Incident start: 2026-06-24 22:41 UTC
- Duration of primary impact: ~42 minutes (service degradation for the generation endpoint used by BrightHealth)
- Impact: increased 5xx error rate and elevated tail latency for model generation requests routed to one autoscaling pool; small fraction (~3%) of production requests returned errors or timed out during that window

Immediate actions taken
- We diverted traffic away from the affected autoscaling pool within 8 minutes of detection to reduce user impact.
- Automated retry and fallback to a compatible model variant were enabled to reduce failed requests.
- On-call and engineering teams collected logs, traces, and a full request timeline; we restored normal service routing by 23:23 UTC.

Preliminary root cause (short version)
- A concurrency bug in the autoscaler’s instance lifecycle handling led to a transient state where KV-cache attachments were not properly rehydrated for some workers during a scale event. This caused a spike in cold-cache latencies and a subset of requests to time out.

Attachments: incident timeline and initial action items (attached) — 2026-06-25-incident-timeline.pdf, mitigation-action-items.xlsx

What we’re doing next (actions and owners)
- Short-term mitigation (completed): traffic diversion and fallback configuration (Evelyn / On-call)
- Medium-term fix (in progress): patch to autoscaler state machine to guarantee KV-cache rehydration ordering; targeted rollout to Dedicated pools in 36 hours (owner: Dev Patel)
- Validation and regression tests: adding CI smoke tests to cover scale events and KV-cache edge cases (owner: Neha Kapoor)
- Customer-facing assurance: we will provide a final RCA and the verification plan once the patch is released; we will also propose a goodwill credit for the impacted window per our SLA. (owner: Stephanie Nguyen)

Request from us
- If you have any specific logs, request IDs, or examples from your side showing failed requests, please send them and we’ll correlate immediately.
- Would you like a short sync (15–20 min) today to walk through the timeline and next steps?

We’ll follow up with an engineering note once the patch is deployed and validated. Apologies again for the disruption — preserving availability and predictable latency is our priority.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Evelyn / team — quick technical update to use in the customer reply:

Root cause (technical detail)
- During a scale-out event, the autoscaler attempted to attach a worker to an existing GPU pool while a concurrent eviction/rebalancing operation was running. A race condition allowed the worker process to begin handling requests prior to the KV-cache rehydration finishing, which produced high tail latencies and intermittent errors for requests that relied on hot prefix cache contents.
- This was compounded by a monitoring blind spot: our health check considered the worker process up but did not validate KV-cache readiness.

Planned fix and rollout
- Code change: add a pre-accept hook in the autoscaler worker lifecycle to block request handling until KV-cache rehydration completes and add explicit readiness probes that validate KV cache consistency.
- Timeline: branch cut now; PR + internal review by 2026-06-25 23:59 UTC; CI + canary rollout to non-production pools 2026-06-26 08:00 UTC; staged rollout to Dedicated pools (including BrightHealth if desired) 2026-06-26 18:00 UTC — full rollout expected within 6 hours of the start of the staged rollout, barring regressions.
- Risk/maintenance window: minimal — staged rollout will be traffic-safe; we will run the canary with higher log verbosity and circuit breakers. Expect occasional transient elevating logs but not customer-facing errors if fallbacks operate as expected.

Verification plan
- Add CI smoke tests that simulate rapid scale events and assert success of KV-cache rehydration.
- Post-deploy: 24-hour monitoring window with a focused log/tracing sweep and an open channel to BrightHealth for any anomalies.

I will provide the PR link and canary IDs once available. If BrightHealth prefers we postpone their Dedicated pool rollout until after their business hours, let me know and we’ll schedule accordingly.

—Dev
